ola-en-01-tip.caption: Ring Ola Accountancy on a Tuesday afternoon and the aim is simple: you start the conversation in the middle, not at the beginning. We are a small team by design and we keep it that way, so the person who picks up is usually the one who did your bookkeeping or filed your last return. They have your business on the screen and they remember what we agreed in September. That matters most on the day you need an answer by four o'clock and you have not got half an hour spare to explain yourself from scratch. A phone call to your accountant should feel like continuing a conversation, not opening a case.
ola-en-01-tip.ask: Worth passing to anyone weighing up accountants this winter.
ola-en-01-tip.title: A phone call that starts in the middle, not at the beginning
ola-en-01-tip.bluesky: A call to your accountant should feel like continuing a conversation, not opening a case. We keep the team small, so the person who picks up is usually the one who did your books.

ola-en-02-acq.caption: You know the question. It is the one you nearly asked out loud, or nearly typed into Google at eleven at night, and then left exactly where it was. Bring that one. The first conversation with us is free and lasts half an hour, and it is a conversation rather than a pitch: you say what you do and what is nagging at you, we tell you in plain English what we would look at first and what sorting it would involve. Afterwards you decide. Working with us is one ending; going away to think about it is a perfectly normal one too. We look after businesses in Luton and the towns around it, and plenty more the length of the UK.
ola-en-02-acq.ask: Keep this somewhere for the week you decide to get it straightened out.
ola-en-02-acq.title: Half an hour, free, for the question you keep leaving alone
ola-en-02-acq.bluesky: The question you nearly asked and then left where it was: bring that one. Half an hour, free, a conversation rather than a pitch, and nothing to sign at the end. Luton, the towns round it, and across the UK.
ola-en-02-acq.gmb:
Ola Accountancy looks after small businesses, sole traders and limited companies in Luton and the towns around it, and clients the length of the UK.

The easiest way to start is a free 30 minute consultation. You tell us what you do and what is worrying you, and we tell you where you stand in plain English. No jargon, no sales script, and nothing to sign at the end of it. People come to us for all sorts of reasons: they want a phone that gets answered by someone who knows their file, the business has grown past the spreadsheet, or they would simply rather not carry the filing dates in their head.

We handle the bookkeeping, the VAT, the payroll, the annual accounts and the Self Assessment tax returns, and we keep the calendar so you do not have to. If you are moving from another accountant we deal with the handover ourselves, including the professional clearance letter to the outgoing firm.

Message us on WhatsApp 0330 133 1886.

ola-en-03-acq.caption: The best version of this is dull. A short email from us in good time, a list of four things we need from you, you send them over, and some weeks later a line saying it has gone to HMRC with a copy attached. That is the service, and it is meant to be unexciting. We keep the calendar: the yearly accounts a limited company has to file, the VAT returns if you are registered for VAT, the payroll each month, and the Self Assessment tax return, which is due by 31 January. A tax return is just the form that tells HMRC what you earned and what you owe on it. Knowing when each one falls due is the part you are paying us to hold.
ola-en-03-acq.ask: One to keep if the dates currently live in your head.
ola-en-03-acq.title: The best version of an accountant is a dull one
ola-en-03-acq.bluesky: The best version of an accountant is dull: an email in good time, a list of four things we need, then a line saying it has gone to HMRC. We hold the calendar, including the tax return due 31 January.

ola-en-04-joke.caption: Every business has one. The invoice went out in August and the payment has been going out on Friday ever since. At some point you stopped being annoyed about it and started finding it funny, which is its own kind of warning sign. The uncomfortable part is that an invoice nobody chases quietly turns into a donation. So put the payment date on the invoice itself, send one reminder before that date and one after it, and if it is still sitting there once the date has gone, ring. None of that is aggressive; it is simply what being owed money looks like in a business that is run properly. The people who pay you on time are usually the ones who know you will notice.
ola-en-04-joke.ask: Forward it to whoever keeps telling you Friday.
ola-en-04-joke.title: The payment that has been going out on Friday since August
ola-en-04-joke.bluesky: The invoice went out in August. The payment has been going out on Friday ever since. You stopped being annoyed and started finding it funny, which is the warning sign. An invoice nobody chases turns into a donation.

ola-en-05-quote.caption: Marcus Aurelius ran an empire and still found it necessary to write this down for himself. Most of us do the same thing on a smaller scale. We plan the better business instead of doing the next hard, dull, useful thing in it: the invoice chased, the receipts filed, the pricing finally put up. The debate is comfortable because nothing changes while it is going on. The work is not comfortable, and it is the only part that counts. Pick the one thing you have been describing instead of doing, and do that today.
ola-en-05-quote.ask: Save this for the next evening you spend planning instead of starting.
ola-en-05-quote.title: Stop describing the business you want and run the one you have
ola-en-05-quote.bluesky: "Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one." Marcus Aurelius. The same goes for the business you keep planning instead of doing the next dull useful thing in it.
